newsitem.title: SPAIN: Demand swamps A.Dominguez in Madrid bourse debut.
newsitem.headline: Demand swamps A.Dominguez in Madrid bourse debut.

text.p: An offer of shares in Spanish design house Adolfo Dominguez has been heavily oversubscribed in the country's first flotation of a quality fashion firm.
Small investor demand has outstripped supply by 75 times on the penultimate day of the bidding period, sale co-ordinators Banco Central Hispano said on Wednesday.
The response from Spanish institutions has been even greater, with bids outstipping by 100 times the number of shares on offer, while the international tranche is 40 times oversubscribed.
This initial public offering is for 70 percent of the fashion firm's capital, or 5.9 million shares, with the portion offered to small investors accounting for roughly 40 percent of the total offer.
Although the venture was expected to be successful, no-one anticipated it would beat stock exchange records, especially amid a spate of government share sales.

Given the strong demand, the price per share is likely to be at the top end of the range initially forecast of between 2,650 pesetas and 3,100 pesetas ($18.30-$21.40). The price will be fixed on Thursday.

The eponymous Galician designer is often credited with having helped to relax Spain's conservative dress-sense during the transition to democracy after the death of dictator General Francisco Franco in 1975.
The Adolfo Dominguez look is most frequently compared with Italy's Giorgio Armani, because of its simple lines and soft colour schemes.

At the start of the 1980s Dominguez earned fame by producing unprecedented crumpled linen designs under the slogan "creases are beautiful". The clothes are still sought after because they are practical but classic-looking.
Much of the success of the flotation was attributed to the charisma of the designer himself.
"Adolfo is a very good salesman and a magnificent communicator. I think that's what's gone down so well with investors," a source close to the operation said.
The design firm posted a net profit of 1.26 billion pesetas in 1996 on sales of 7.53 billion pesetas, and analysts forecast 25 percent annual profit growth for the next three years.
The company's range is produced via a vertical structure, aimed at minimising risk in what is generally considered to be a fickle business.

The structure integrates design, production and sales, retailing via its own shops and franchises in 72 outlets including in Britain, France, Portugal and Japan. Sales abroad accounted for 19.8 percent of the total in 1996.
The shares will start trade in Madrid on March 18. ($ = 144.8 Spanish Pesetas)
